entries.title: Mark 10:1
segments: Beyond the Jordan. Perea.  Between the end of chapter 9 and the beginning of chapter 10 Mark omits several events.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:2
segments: Is it lawful, etc.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:5
segments: For your hardness of heart. Christ rebukes their false standard as to the sacredness of the marriage relation.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:9
segments: What therefore God hath joined together. See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:10
segments: And in the house. Perplexed by the moral rigor and purity of Christ's commands, the disciples sought more light on the question.  They had already done so on more than one occasion (
).  They themselves had been brought up in a more lax view of marriage than that announced authoritatively by our Lord.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:13
segments: Bringing unto him little children. According to custom.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:17
segments: There ran one to him. The rich young man who had kept the commandments, but lacked the courage to sell all he had and give to the poor.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:24
segments: How hard is it for them that trust in riches. This utterance of our Lord regarding the destructive power of riches on the spiritual life is even more emphatic than the words in
, or in
.  It points out the reason why it is so difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God-because his trust is in his riches.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:26
segments: They were astonished exceedingly. The compassion of Jesus for all who suffered, and his tender care of his disciples, often seemed to the latter in sharp contrast to the inflexible severity of his moral principles and commands.  But when they were thus astonished and perplexed, he was always ready to point out the way of escape, as in
.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:28
segments: Peter began to say. Peter's words here seem to indicate that he too was not free from the taint of undue love of riches.  He asked, evidently not with the highest motive, 'what then shall we have?' (
).  The reply of Jesus affirms all the fullness of earthly as well as heavenly reward for those who are true to him; but he adds, 'with persecutions.'

entries.title: Mark 10:32
segments:
On the way. The main road that led to Jerusalem.
 

 
Was going before them. In the position of authority as well as danger--leader, guide, shepherd.  He was proceeding to the scene of his suffering and death.

entries.title: Mark 10:33
segments: Shall deliver him unto the Gentiles. It was the Roman power that carried out the sentence of death.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 10:37
segments: Grant unto us. See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:40
segments: For whom it hath been prepared. That is, the question you ask does not now concern your position and your needs and will be finally decided in due time.

entries.title: Mark 10:41
segments: Began to be moved with indignation. At the presumption of James and John in trying to secure the highest position for themselves.  Their father Zebedee was wealthier than the parents of the other apostles, and probably they considered that they had stronger claims to advancement.

entries.title: Mark 10:43
segments: It is not so among you. You are not to imitate the cruel pride of force and brutal authority which obtains among the Gentiles.  You are under a higher law, the law of unselfish service.

entries.title: Mark 10:45
segments: A ransom for many. The supreme proof of his right to be ruler in the kingdom of God.  He gave most for us, therefore most righteously does he rule over us.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 10:46
segments: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar Matthew says there were two blind men.  Only one is mentioned here, probably because he was better known.  See notes on
